content:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate — p99 latency crossed 3s threshold (region: us-west-2). triggered by 5m spike. severity: Sev2

pagerduty: paging Nina (oncall) and eng-sre rotation — incident created PD-4821. escalate if no ack in 5m. :rotating_light:

Nina (oncall): got it, looking. seeing requests backlog in the streaming router. start of spike ~ 1777777600 per prom query.

Sara K: I can join — looks like GPU nodes in pool-inference-gpu-07 are spiking temp and IO. saw a few ECC corrected errors in node logs.

Mike T: can you paste the prom queries you ran? I want to check p95/p99 and streaming stall metrics.

Sara K: prom query I used:
```
max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,job))[10m:1m])
```
graph shows p99 ~ 4.8s at peak, p95 ~ 1.2s. Streaming stall counter (streaming_chunk_sent_failures) jumped x7.

Raj P: on the node itself I ran `nvidia-smi` — temps are in the high 90s C and GPU utilization is erratic:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d TEMPERATURE,ERROR
GPU 0: Temp 97 C, Performance State P2
ECC errors (corrected): 14
GPU 1: Temp 92 C, Thermal slow down engaged
```
kernel dmesg shows repeated RAS/ECC corrections and some PCIe link retrains.

Alyssa L: That matches the runtime logs — we've had retries on the CUDA IPC channel and KV cache misses causing reinitialization on some requests. Streaming path waits on KV regen and stalls the chunking goroutine.

Nina (oncall): initial mitigation plan: 1) mark the suspect node(s) drain-only, 2) route new requests away, 3) scale up warm spare pool (if available), 4) reduce batching thresholds to prefer latency, 5) open customer comms if impact > 5%.

Sara K: I'm going to cordon & drain the node. command: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-07 && kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

eng-sre-bot: TASK queued: drain started for gpu-node-07 (initiated by Sara K). Estimated 2m to evict pods.

Mike T: lowering batch size via config param `max_batch_tokens=1024` -> was 4096. Pushing config to edge routers now.

Raj P: also flipping per-pod env flag to disable async KV prefetch for affected nodes — that'll reduce pressure on IPC but might slightly increase token compute.

Alyssa L: I'm watching streaming chunk metrics. stalls per min dropping after drain begin. p99 trending down from 4.8s -> 2.6s within three minutes. p95 down to ~0.9s.

Nina (oncall): good. I'm going to mark this incident as mitigated if no customer-facing errors in next 10m. Please keep an eye on ECC counts and thermal events.

Sara K: Node logs after drain:
```
[ 00:12:43 ] ECC corrected errors count increased rapidly: +9
[ 00:12:46 ] Thermal throttling engaged on GPU 0
[ 00:12:50 ] Driver reported GPU reset on GPU 0, process MIGRATION triggered
```
We should RMA that GPU or take node out of rotation until hardware check.

Mike T: I'm going to backfill traffic to dedicated-reserve pool to avoid overloaded spare nodes. rerouting now: `route-policy set --route inference=dedicated-reserve --weight 0.6`

eng-sre-bot: Deployment change applied. Routing weight updated.

Raj P: quick note — I enabled temporary kernel parameter to be less aggressive on ECC logging to reduce interrupt storms: `echo 1 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/ecc_log_throttle` (temporary, will revert).

Nina (oncall): customer impact assessment: ~8% of requests experienced >2s additional latency window during the 5m spike. No request errors returned to customers, only elevated latency and streaming stalls. No SLO credits yet but need PM notification.

Alyssa L: alerting: raising a ticket to product-alerts channel to draft a status update for impacted customers.

Sara K: after draining, p99 stabilized around 1.1s and streaming stalls back to baseline. Node still showing persistent corrected ECC counts — not safe to bring back.

Nina (oncall): handing off oncall to Mike T for follow-up (next shift). key action items:
- Mike: coordinate hardware RMA / open ticket with datacenter and schedule replacement.
- Raj: collect and attach GPU diagnostics (nvidia-smi -q, dmesg, collect /var/log/nvidia-driver).
- Sara: add postmortem stub and link to incident board. include suggested mitigations: thermal alarms earlier, stricter node health gating, automatic drain on ECC > threshold.

Mike T: acked. I'll open DC ticket now and coordinate RMA.

Raj P: uploading diagnostics bundle to /tmp/incidents/PD-4821-diagnostics.tar.gz and linking to the incident board.

eng-sre-bot: bundle uploaded: https://redwood.internal/storage/incidents/PD-4821-diagnostics.tar.gz

Nina (oncall): marking incident as "mitigated" at 1777777899. We'll run a full postmortem and share within 48h. If any regression in next 24h escalate immediately.

Alyssa L: adding retrospective items: add p99 early warning, trigger cordon when ECC corrected > 10 within 5m, add thermal threshold alert at 85C.

Sara K: thanks everyone. Follow-ups: RMA ticket #DC-9182 (opened), postmortem draft at /docs/incidents/PD-4821-draft.md.

Mike T: closing loop with customer success after postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: PD-4821 status changed to mitigated. Participants: Nina (oncall), Sara K, Raj P, Mike T, Alyssa L.

Nina (oncall): handing off to Mike — I will be offline for next hour. ping me if rollback needed. :wave:
